subject: Post-demo: Benchmarking playbook, reproducibility checklist, and next steps
messages:
From: Sam Knox <sam.knox@novusretail.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Varga <elena.varga@novusretail.com>
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Demo follow-up + perf SLOs

Marcus — thanks again for the demo this morning. Quick recap from our side and the perf-related asks we want to validate before moving forward:

- Goal: conversational product for customer support (streaming responses) and a content-generation batch job.
- SLO targets (initial): p95 latency <= 180 ms for single-turn streaming responses (up to 512 tokens), sustained throughput to support 50 concurrent active users (concurrency measured as simultaneous open chat sessions), and peak batch throughput ~ 2000 requests/hour for summarization jobs (non-streaming).
- Determinism: for evaluation we need reproducible runs (same prompt set, fixed sampling) to compare quality across model variants.

Attached: Novus_prod_sample_prompts_v1.csv (prompt families + expected output examples).

Next steps we discussed: share your benchmark methodology (how you measure latency/throughput), a short reproducibility checklist, and a proposed timeline for a qualification benchmark. Can you also confirm whether Redwood will run the bench on hosted infra (recommended) or if we should set aside a Dedicated pool?

Thanks — Sam
Sam Knox
Head of Platforms, Novus Retail
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Knox <sam.knox@novusretail.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 11:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo follow-up + perf SLOs

Sam — great to see the prompt set, thanks. Below is a short benchmarking playbook and an initial plan so we can get a qualification run scheduled early next week. I attached a concise playbook (redwood_bench_playbook.pdf) and a sample harness config (sample_eval_harness.yaml).

High-level plan (two phases):
1) Qualification run (48–72 hours): lightweight, reproducible small-scale run against your prompt families to validate p95/p99 latency and streaming behavior. This is what we use to validate SLO feasibility.
2) Full-run (24–48 hours continuous): larger stress profile with concurrency ramps, warm-up windows, and production-like token distributions to compute steady-state throughput and cost estimates.

Measurement definitions (summary):
- Latency: server-to-client time for first byte (TTFB) for streaming, plus time to final token for non-streaming. We report p50/p90/p95/p99 over the measurement window (after warm-up).
- Throughput: tokens/sec aggregated per model instance and global throughput over the run window.
- Concurrency: concurrent active sessions measured as open websocket/stream connections.
- Errors: 4xx/5xx counts, OOMs, model timeouts, truncated responses.

Reproducibility checklist (summary): seed + sampling params, model version + quantization, env (CUDA version, GPU type), batch size, cache warm-up policy, exact prompt tokenization. See attached checklist for full details.

What we need from Novus to get started:
- Confirm which prompt set(s) from the CSV to include in the qualification run (recommend a representative 200 prompts across families).
- Provide target sampling parameters (temperature/top_p) for evaluation and a note whether deterministic runs (temperature=0 / greedy) are acceptable for quality diffs.
- Access: either a short-lived S3 location for the prompt set or allow us to pull the CSV from a shared Drive link.
- Preferred window: we can run qualification as early as Mon 2 Jun (US day) if we lock in access and sampling params by Fri 29 May EOD.

We typically run the qualification on Hosted Redwood infra first (faster turnaround). If you need production-like numbers on Dedicated, we'll schedule a Dedicated slot for the full-run (there's additional lead time).

I'll let Lauren and Priyom add the technical run parameters; happy to hop on a quick call if you'd like to walk through the playbook.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Knox <sam.knox@novusretail.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo follow-up + perf SLOs — technical clarifications

Adding a few concrete bench definitions so the qualification run is reproducible and compares apples-to-apples across model variants: 

Benchmarking specifics we recommend (please confirm):
- Prompt tokenization: use BPE tokenizer version X from the model repo; record token counts in results.
- Sampling for quality regression: for diffing we recommend temperature=0 (deterministic) on a 200-prompt eval; separate stochastic runs (temp=0.7, top_p=0.95) for human-eval quality checks.
- Streaming: stream-first-byte target = 120ms median, 180ms p95 on 512-token context. We emit partial chunks every 200ms or ~32 tokens (whichever comes first). Measurement for streaming p95 uses time-to-first-chunk and time-to-final-token separately.
- Warm-up: 5 minutes or 500 requests, whichever comes first, before measuring steady-state. Document KV-cache warm-up policy: for chat flows with long context (>=2048 tokens) do a synthetic warm-up that populates KV cache for the typical context length.
- Concurrency ramping: linear ramp from 1 to target concurrency over 10 minutes, hold for 30 minutes, then ramp down; repeat for two cycles during the full-run.
- Metrics: p50/p90/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, requests/sec, CPU/GPU util, memory and GPU memory usage, cost-per-1M-tokens estimate, and error rate. Include raw traces (request id ↔ timestamps) for reproducibility.
- Environment capture: record model binary hash, quantization profile (e.g., 8-bit GPTQ), runtime kernel versions, CUDA/cuDNN, GPU type (A100v4), and Redwood runtime version.

On reproducibility: we will run the same harness code and provide the harness config (sample_eval_harness.yaml) you can review. For your part, if you can provide any batch post-processing rules (truncation, stop tokens), list those explicitly so outputs match.

If all good, we'll proceed with the qualification run on Mon 2 Jun. Otherwise, flag any of the above items and we'll adapt.

—Lauren
Principal Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Sam Knox <sam.knox@novusretail.com>

Subject: Re: Demo follow-up + perf SLOs — technical clarifications

Thanks Lauren — this is quite thorough and aligns with our needs. A few quick clarifications from our infra team:

- Deterministic runs: yes please start with temperature=0 for the baseline diffs. We'll run human-eval stochastic checks separately.
- Streaming chunking: 200ms chunk cadence works. We'll accept p95 first-byte <= 180ms for the qualification run but need a path to 120–150ms for production.
- Access: Elena will share an S3 pre-signed URL with the prompt CSV and sample labels by EOD Fri.
- Dedicated vs hosted: for the qualification run, hosted is fine. If qualification looks good, we'll request a Dedicated pilot for the full-run and eventual production (legal procurement + contract).

One ask on timelines: can you confirm the expected turnaround from end of qualification to a full-run slot estimate and an updated cost ballpark? Also, do you have a simple reproducibility report template we can fill for future audits?

Sam
